newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps - CFDs jump 12 cts into backwardation.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps - CFDs jump 12 cts into backwardation.

text.p: European oil swaps mostly gained on Monday although jet swaps stayed at depressed levels after losing ground on Friday.
Brent crude CFDs jumped 12 cents a barrel to talk close to five cents over July for this weeks dates while the next three weeks were backwardated by about four or five cents a week.
The 27-30 May week traded three cents above the 2-6 June week but no outright trades were heard. Despite the backwardation on weekly CFDs, monthly CFDs priced against the IPE remained in contango.
June was valaued at 13 cents under the screen while July was nearer eight cents.
Gasoline gained $1 a tonne to talk around $199.50 for both May and June. July was $3 a tonne lower and physical barges traded at just $197.50 for loading by 20 May.
Crack spreads were unchanged at $4.10 a barrel and $3.10 for the third and fourth quarters respectively.
Heavy fuel also firmed $1 a tonne to $86.50 for May barges but little trade was heard. June was seen at parity with low sulphur holding some $5 a tonne higher.
Dealers said the strength largely reflected gains made in recent days in Singapore. Local demand for bunker fuel and from Italy for low sulphur were subdued.

Further forward the contango showed signs of flattening out. The third to fourth quarter contango fell to $4.50 a tonne from $5.50 on Wednesday. The two quarters were valued at $87 and $91.50 respectively.

Jet premiums stayed depressed after sinking $1 to $2 a tonne on Friday. June and July held at $20 a tonne and $22 a tonne above the IPE respectively. While the winter months were still pegged at $29 above the screen, having traded that level on Friday.
Gas oil crack spreads held at $4.30 a barrel (3Q97), $4.85 (4Q97) and $4.75 (1Q98). -- Sam Arnold-Forster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4984
